items.title: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, more: What AppleInsider thinks about 'Surprise and Shine'
items.summary: It's been a busy few days. In the fallout of the iPhone Duo reveal at the "Surprise and Shine" event, we have some thoughts. What are yours?
items.content_html:
It's been a busy few days. In the fallout of the iPhone Duo reveal at the "Surprise and Shine" event, we have some thoughts. What are yours?

The 77 minute event was bookended by the latest iPhone models, a bunch of Apple Health updates related to more powerful Apple Watches, and a smidge on AirPods 5. Tim Cook made a cameo, Johnny Srouji had a sore throat, and yes, there's a foldable iPhone.

The AppleInsider staff comes in many shapes, sizes, and opinions that run the gamut. For every devout staffer hyped about the latest release, there's a skeptic worried about the implications.

Here's what the staff thought, and perhaps if they're ready to share, what they plan on buying.

William Gallagher - Duo is blinding

All I can say for certain is that the iPhone Duo means I've no interest at all now in the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Other than that, I vacillate between wanting to buy an iPhone Duo and then really seriously doubting why.

iPhone Duo was the star of the show

Cost is of course a factor but what most prevents me deciding to buy is how the opened-up screen will feel in use. Some of the actors in Apple's video looked a little awkward holding that wide screen in one hand while tapping away with the other.

Like with the iPad, developers will have to fix their apps to take advantage of the Duo's new proportions. Web developers will have to work to make their sites look good on the unit.

So, those are all usability concerns. All iPhone apps look terrible on iPad, if they didn't get updated.

I'm also unsure about how it will feel when closed. It's definitely squat and somehow that feels like a compromise. The question is whether I would use it most open or closed and I cannot figure that out right now.

But it does come in blue, so.

Apple Watch Series 12 made an appearance at the event too

Still, I fixated on the iPhone Duo for myself, but it was actually the Apple Watch that I immediately talked with friends about. I've friends who use various medical wearables and it seemed to me that the new Apple Watch Series 12 could do at least a lot of what they like.

One is thinking about it and I've told her to just give me the nod when she wants a present.

Apparently there were also AirPods at the event but they didn't really even register with me. I do like that the noise cancelling version costs less than the previous version, but that's really because everyone should have active noise cancellation in their lives.

Wesley Hilliard - cautious foldable convert

For whatever reason the iPhone Duo name didn't leak in any real way until hours before the Apple Event. It was such a well-kept secret, I wondered if it would ever release, let alone be announced in September.

iPhone Duo is real and it's an interesting new product from Apple

As June came and went with more hints about a foldable hidden in code, I made a call — if there is an iPhone Fold, I need to buy one to evaluate. Lo and behold, Apple revealed the iPhone Duo.

Before I go further, the rest of the event went great.

I loved the Cook appearance even if the opening video was among Apple's least interesting. AirPods 5 definitely exist, and I'm certain most of the Apple Watch section was about features coming to everyone, though the new hardware has key improvements.

As I watched the iPhone 18 Pro reveal with variable aperture and a more powerful chipset, I was deeply afraid I was about to miss out on an excellent upgrade. As someone that loves photography, I find it very important to carry the best possible camera with me, and that's always been iPhone in the past decade.

The new variable aperture system uses a rotor to control shutter blades thinner than hair

Variable aperture is such a useful idea even if the range only goes from f/1.48 to f/4.0. Apple's example photos are incredible, of course, but I do wonder how this feature would actually affect day-to-day shooting.

Sadly, I won't be able to find out, because I'm ordering the iPhone Duo. When CEO John Ternus stepped out to reveal his "one more thing," I forgot all of my reservations and was ready to be excited.

The iPhone Duo is stunning. Apple's specialty of blending hardware and software is front and center with this product. It seems Apple has even found a way to virtually eliminate the crease and hide what may exist from view thanks to nano texture.

An opening and closing animation makes the dual displays feel more connected

Everything about this product depends on the software experience, and the rethought iOS shows Apple really thought this out. I can only hope developers support the platform in a way they never bothered with Apple Vision Pro.

Luckily, supporting iPhone Duo is significantly more straightforward.

Even the camera system is well implemented from general photography use to FaceTime calls. The Fusion Main camera appears to be the same camera system, sans variable aperture, offered with iPhone 18 Pro, and the Fusion Ultra Wide is identical.

I was ready to buy a dedicated point-and-shoot camera to supplement what could have been a bad camera experience. Apple may have convinced me not to with iPhone Duo, but you'll have to wait for the review to see if they've succeeded.

I ordered Apple Watch Ultra 4 and will attempt to get a release-day shipment of the iPhone Duo.

Amber Neely - Fighting off marketing

By this point in the game, most of you know that I don't upgrade frequently. Hopefully, you already know that I'm not easily swayed by marketing.

Not even John Ternus can win everyone over to the iPhone Duo

In fact, after seven years at AppleInsider and at least a dozen Apple events, these sorts of presentations just bounce off of me. I watch events the same way Cypher read code in "The Matrix."

Instead of seeing blondes, brunettes, and redheads, though, I see "too expensive, too gimmicky, appealing to the Everyman."

It's probably as much of a superpower as Mike being able to predict a new Star Trek episode's plot in the first five minutes for the last 30 years. It does help me retain my residency as one of the more Apple-critical writers on staff.

John Ternus did a pretty okay Tim Cook impression. We'll see if he develops his own personality in a few years or so.

I'm one of those people who is wary of marketing hype. After careful assessment, I'll care about a device, any device, once I get it, if I get it.

The iPhone 18 Pro is tempting for some, but won't justify an upgrade for all

I own an iPhone 17, and I do not need to upgrade. My iPhone 17 will be perfectly serviceable until probably 2029.

Now, here's where the twist comes in: I still might upgrade. And the worst part is that I might upgrade to the iPhone Duo.

I'd have to really budget for it, but I am interested in the iPhone Duo. I'm sure Mike finds this particularly amusing, as I've long decried the idea of a foldable phone.

The crease will happen. That should be a deal breaker for me alone.

However, I also like small phones, and you don't get smaller than the iPhone Duo. And it'll be compatible with the Apple Pencil.

I am, at my core, still an iPad girlie. And the idea of being able to whip out my phone and turn it into an iPad at a moment's notice is pretty tempting.

Check back in six months to see whether Apple managed to bully $2,000 out of me.

Mike Wuerthele - The cycle repeats

I'm tired. I'm not submarine-duty tired, but I'm also not as young as I was then.

This is my 15th flagship iPhone event working for a publication that's facing the internet, and I've done every single one of them in one reporting capacity or another. Each one has good points, each one has yawners, and even from day one, there has always been a surprise or two.

The iPhone 18 Pro is, as expected, iterative. It's got variable aperture, and a better vapor chamber cooling system, sure. That's cool, I guess.

AirPods were a little bit of a surprise. In a world where every single electronic device is getting hiked (looking at you, $250 Apple TV), a refresh with more, coming in for less money than the previous version, is refreshing. And, the sales on these for Christmas are going to be spectacular.

The Apple Watch is yet another iterative year, which is fine. There's a reason Apple spent like 10 minutes tops on the product line.

It does what it says it will do, and as an all-rounder, it's best in class. I'm still a little bitter that my original Apple Watch Ultra got cut off from some features so quickly, but it's not the first time that's happened, and won't be the last.

In this gig, the rumor mill leading up to release isn't a carrot, it's a stick, that's frequently beating you atop the head and shoulders. The stoppers and features get talked about for sometimes years, like for the Duo.

iPhone Duo shows Apple knows when to pull out all of the stops

The iPhone Duo is impressive. I watched the same address that you all did, and am getting information as we discover it from Andrew at the event.

Apple technology unchained, is always interesting and polarizing. There are already complaints that this will be an Apple Vision Pro "debacle," but that's not a good take.

Apple Vision Pro was a product in search of a market for exorbitant prices. The iPhone Duo is landing in a well-established market, with buyers that have been clamoring for more, for another form factor, for years. And coming in at $1999 to start, it is cheaper than industry observers thought it would be.

It will define the foldable category. Single-handedly, it will at least double the scope of the market.

If you have a substantial iCloud Family, you should look at the very briefly announced Apple One Family. Yeah, $50 a month is a lot, but it'll cover everything you own that's eligible, and what the rest of your family owns too, automatically. We've already done some math about it, but do your own calculations before you jump.

As for what I'm buying? I don't know yet. My M5 Max Mac Studio will be here shortly, since I got somebody to buy my M1 Ultra Mac Studio to completely finance the purchase, so I've got some mad money. That, and my veteran's discount is nice.

I don't want to be in the market for an iPhone 18 Pro, because my personal iPhone 16 Pro is fine. If that dies, I have AppleCare One Individual, so I'm good to go for a bit.

I'll have access to a friend's iPhone Duo right after it ships. I hope it doesn't awaken feelings in me, because as a Mac-first worker, that seduction would be expensive, and I would not get as much out as I could.

Apple's push into foldables is another in a long line of big industry moves

Oh, and one more thing from me. Every main iPhone event is rumored to have all the updates for everything. HomePods, the Home Hub, the Apple TV, and more were all anticipated by some for this one. That was never realistic, this was always going to be 75 minutes and out, with the folding iPhone the centerpiece.

Those all are for the future, that starts right after the new desktop Macs ship. It's going to be a pretty busy six months.

Maybe I'll get some rest afterwards. Or maybe right after WWDC 2027.

items.title: Ternus and Joswiak talk about designing the iPhone Duo in secret
items.summary: In a new interview, Apple CEO John Ternus talks about the long road to the iPhone Duo, while Joz is delighted just how secret they kept the project.
items.content_html:
In a new interview, Apple CEO John Ternus talks about the long road to the iPhone Duo, while Joz is delighted just how secret they kept the project.

It had been rumored for such a long time, and so many leaks got little details right, but overall the iPhone Duo has been Apple's best-kept secret in years. Talking to Tom's Guide and TechRadar in a new interview, Greg Joswiak, senior vice president of worldwide marketing, says he's "super proud" of that.

"We put extra security on it, we didn't talk about it to anyone," he said. "We had a very funny codename, which I won't even repeat, that had nothing to do with it."

"People knew through leaks that we were working on a foldable [and] unfortunately they got the aspect ratio," he continued, "[but] this is one, we said, okay, we're gonna really keep this one locked down, and it worked."

Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

New Apple CEO John Ternus says that there came a point in all of the design work when Apple thought "yes, that's it."

"This is what happens, we always know we're on the right track when you get that first design model or prototype and you go, oh, this is it, right?" said Ternus. "This is what I want. And then once we have that, then it's like, okay, how do we make it happen and make it real?"

Part of making it real, though, did involve talking to people outside of Apple. "We went out a little bit broader than we might normally in reaching out to our third-party developers," said Joz, "to have them do some work as to how they are going to take advantage of [the iPhone Duo]."

"We had no problem getting anybody to come in and want to do this," he continued. "There was a lot of enthusiasm."

The first $2,000 iPhone

AppleInsider has used the new iPhone Duo in person and couldn't really be more enthusiastic about it. But there is still the fact that it is the most expensive iPhone ever made.

"Look, we're always focused on, obviously, building cool things that people love, but also are really good value, right?" said Ternus. "And this is an incredibly, like, complex and well-engineered device."

"So far the response suggests [that] a lot of people are really excited about it, but one of the great things about our lineup now is that there's kind of different devices for different people's priorities," he continued.

Speaking to this point of the price and the value, Joz had the straightforward answer that iPhone Duo is both an iPhone and an iPad.

"I mean, it's called iPhone Duo for a reason... it is, like, two products, right?" he said. "It's like your iPhone, your familiar experience that you're used to, [but] open it up to this massive display, and it's a whole new experience, a whole new world."

Both men also enthused about the new iPhone 18 Pro and how that will be the right model for some people. Read AppleInsider's breakdown of the benefits and disadvantages of both the iPhone Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro.

items.title: Tim Cook's cameo in the iPhone Duo launch was pure television drama
items.summary: After all the seemingly obvious reports that Tim Cook would not be in the new iPhone launch video, there he was. He was there for a purpose, and he was there because yet again, only Apple could do this.
items.content_html:
After all the seemingly obvious reports that Tim Cook would not be in the new iPhone launch video, there he was. He was there for a purpose, and he was there because yet again, only Apple could do this.

That's because while there must be countless CEOs who insist on being the star of their corporate videos, there aren't many with the public profile of Tim Cook. You could well argue that his making a cameo in the new iPhone veent was ego, but it felt as if it were more about the viewer than the man.

And there were so many viewers. Within an hour of the presentation finishing, YouTube was showing that 26 million people had watched.

They're not all AppleInsider readers, they're not all technology fans. Instead, the giant majority would be people who are interested in the company's products, and who know that Apple puts on a good show.

These are not people who would necessarily have learned that Tim Cook was stepping down in advance, although he got worldwide coverage at the news the day it happened. They are not people who would already know who his successor was and go "oh, right, that Ternus guy."

So while Cook's cameo would make little sense to someone watching an Apple video for the first time, for most people this was when the succession happened. This was the Doctor Who-like regeneration, with John Ternus stepping in to bring a new take on a familiar role.

iPhone launch as a show

This is polarizing, here, even amongst our staff.

Since Apple moved from live presentations to pre-recorded videos, it has done a genuinely superb job at shaping the whole show. It's much more complex than just rolling out a series of presenters to the same stage, but it never looks like it is.

The last time Tim Cook appeared to step down, he ended up in a "Severance" promo video - image credit: Apple.

We're used to seeing Apple presenters speak from places around the world. In some years, it's even all designed so that the first presenters are shown in morning sunlight, and the last ones are at night.

Maybe that's a callback to how long the live presentations used to be.

In this case, Apple even directly acknowledged that it was making a show. It opened with a series of fantastically-well filmed and way over-budgeted clips of people describing the best ways to open such a show.

It wasn't 100% effective, though, starting with how if you were a long-time viewer, it was a near repeat of Steven Spielberg's intro to the Apple TV+ launch back in 2019.

Then just as with the over-extended "Mother Nature" sketch in 2023, this opener outstayed its welcome. The same idea was repeated six times before we got to the main one, the voiceover talking us through a zoom into Apple Park.

Finally there was the climax, with the big reveal of the presenter, Tim Cook. He got the famous Captain Kirk shot from original Star Trek, too. Cook is mostly in shadow and there's just a dramatic light across his eyes.

But then he chuckles, says "no, no, no, no, not me."

Cook then gestures back to someone behind him to the far distance, and adds "That's your guy."

Tim Cook then exited frame and had one more line tying this all back to the repeated gag about how best to start a video. "That's your opener," he says, wrapping up his last appearance, and also the 2 minute and 36 second-long intro video.

The baton was passed in the most public way it could be. It was like every spin-off TV drama with a familiar character guest-starring to help bring across fans of the old show.

It was legitimizing the opening moments of the new series. That's all a guest cameo can ever do, though, and it's up to the new show to keep viewers watching.

Which John Ternus did as effortlessly as if he'd done this a dozen times before. Mind you, everyone expected a folding iPhone so few were likely to stop watching this time.

items.title: Apple rolls out tvOS 27 with support for video podcasts, improved audio
items.summary: Apple's tvOS 27 update brings a redesigned Podcasts app, better Apple Music audio, new accessibility features, and a handful of smaller improvements to Apple TV.
items.content_html:
Apple's tvOS 27 update brings a redesigned Podcasts app, better Apple Music audio, new accessibility features, and a handful of smaller improvements to Apple TV.

As you know by now, Apple TV updates are somewhat modest compared to other Apple products. That's especially true after the major Liquid Glass redesign introduced with tvOS 26.

Still, tvOS 27 has a few worthwhile additions, particularly for Apple Music and Podcasts users. Here's what Apple's rolling out to the Apple TV.

Podcasts gets a major overhaul

The Apple Podcasts app is getting one of the biggest changes in tvOS 27.

Apple has completely redesigned Podcasts for the Apple TV, adding a new sidebar that makes it easier to navigate through the app and browse shows.

The bigger change is support for video podcasts. Video podcasts are already supported on other platfroms, but tvOS 27 brings that experience to Apple TV.

Smart downloads are also coming to Apple TV. This allows podcast content to be downloaded automatically so that episodes are ready to play when needed.

Apple Music adds new audio features

Apple Music is getting a few improvements in tvOS 27, including support for Hi-Res Lossless audio.

Apple is also bringing AutoMix to Apple Music on both Apple TV and HomePod via tvOS 27. AutoMix uses transitions between songs to make playlists flow more continuously, rather than simply stopping one track before starting the next.

Accessibility improvements

tvOS 27 adds a long-requested accessibility feature with support for larger text.

Users can increase the size of onscreen text through the accessibility settings, making menus and other information easier to read from across the room.

Quality and performance upgrades

Of course, Apple has also been working to improve the overall experience of tvOS in this newest update.

Most notably, animations and app launches are smoother. Control Center is also more responsive.

How to update your Apple TV to tvOS 27

  1. On an Apple TV, go to the Settings, app
  2. Select System
  3. Select Software Updates
  4. Select Update Software

How to update your HomePod or HomePod mini

  1. Ensure your device is updated to the latest version of iOS, iPadOS, or macOS.
  2. Open the Home app
  3. Tap or click ...
  4. Tap or click Home Settings
  5. Tap or click Software Update
  6. If available, tap or click Update

items.title: Apple Watch heart rate accuracy vs. rivals: devil is in the details
items.summary: Apple wasn't kidding when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 12 has the best heart rate accuracy of all wearables, but the extensive study also shows just how close some key rivals are under certain test conditions.
items.content_html:
Apple wasn't kidding when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 12 has the best heart rate accuracy of all wearables, but the extensive study also shows just how close some key rivals are under certain test conditions.

Other than the return of the popular ceramic casing, the Apple Watch Series 12's most significant update was in its improved health sensing system. Central to this is how the new Series 12 and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 monitor heart rate every five seconds.

Apple's Deidre Caldbeck, senior director of Apple Watch and health product marketing, said during the launch that the company had tested it against rivals. Now Apple has published the results of that test.

Naturally it wouldn't have published the results if it weren't true that the Apple Watch comes out top. But deep in the detail, Apple has published just where rivals meet or exceed it in certain areas.

The tests involved 1,460 people who wore a Polar H10 ECG chest strap as reference. Then at the same time, they would wear an Apple Watch on one wrist, while on the other hand they had one of the following:

  • Garmin Forerunner 970
  • Google Pixel Watch 4
  • Huawei Watch 5
  • Oura Ring 5
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 8
  • WHOOP 5

All of these, apart from the Apple Watch, monitor heart rate more during workouts. In those, the Garmin Forerunner 970 measured heart rate much more often, doing so between every 0.25 and 0.5 seconds.

The most significant improvements in Apple Watch concern health - image credit: Apple.

The Huawei Watch 5, Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, and WHOOP 5 all measured heart rate every 2 seconds. The Oura Ring 5 and Google Pixel Watch 4 measured every 5 seconds, like the Apple Watch.

Things change considerably when a user is not exercising, or at least they do for the Samsung and the Oura. The Galaxy Watch 8 only checks once per minute, and while the Oura Ring varies, it's measuring around every 300 seconds.

As well as the rate of measurement, Apple's test included examining accuracy. For this, Apple Watch "demonstrated a statistically significant higher level of accuracy" in categories called overall workout and overall daily living.

It also had "better accuracy for session-level average heart rate" in most of 12 categories that were tested. It wasn't strictly speaking beaten in any of those tests, but Apple says its margin of victory over the Huawei Watch 5 was not statistically significant in a workout test.

Also in eight tests over activities such as cycling and strength testing, Apple Watch did show "better accuracy for the majority of devices in most activities." But for those eight, the conclusions were indeterminate.

One place where Apple admits to being beaten is in what it called a daily living protocol. Again eight conclusions were statistically indeterminate, but in one case the Pixel Watch 4 showed higher accuracy.

That was for what Apple describes as a rest condition only. Apple then stresses that this greater accuracy was "less than a margin of 0.5" beats per minute.

Where else Apple Watch wins

Apple obviously includes health sensing hardware, but it also works to make that data accessible for the user. There's the whole Health app, plus the ability to export the data to doctors if wanted.

That also made it easy to measure the results across all of the tests, and that wasn't the case with every device. According to Apple's research study, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 would only export minimal time stamps "and a single additional heart rate value whose derivation is not documented."

Then the Oura Ring simply wasn't tested during strength training. That's reportedly because the manufacturer recommends not even wearing the ring during weightlifting.

Apple's report gives more detail for the testing methodology, plus a finer breakdown of every result. Ultimately what it tells us is that all wearables provide significant health features, but again it is reportedly true that Apple Watch is overall the most accurate.

This report follows one from January 2026, where a study praised the Apple Watch's usefulness in identifying atrial fibrillation in asymptomatic patients.

items.title: Hands on: Why did iPhone Duo have to be this good?
items.summary: I had a lot of reservations about Apple making a foldable iPhone, but after playing around with iPhone Duo at the Apple Event, I think I'm sold.
items.content_html:
I had a lot of reservations about Apple making a foldable iPhone, but after playing around with iPhone Duo at the Apple Event, I think I'm sold.

A foldable device is cool, but comes with a lot of compromises. I knew, based on the rumors, I was going to be on the fence.

That was before I got the chance to try it out for myself. It wasn't long, but in my time with it, I can easily see it being my daily driver.

Solid, reliable hardware

There will surely be plenty of stress testing post-launch, but right now, it seems like Apple's hardware is solid.

Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

Apple is using a polished titanium frame that will resist scratching while improving durability. It uses a custom hinge with over 100 individual components that help support the inner display when it is open.

It even sports IP68 water and dust resistance, something the latest Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 doesn't have. That gives me a lot of confidence in the strength of this device.

The iPhone Duo laying down with the matte interior screen and no crease

When you open the phone, there is an extremely slight dip on the inner display where the crease is, but it's basically imperceptible. The center of this display feels strong and doesn't flex if you push on it.

Plus, it supports MagSafe, even though early rumors claimed it wouldn't. That likely would have been a dealbreaker for me.

We have some concerns about MagSafe accessory fit, but more on that a bit later on September 10.

iPhone Duo camera tricks

One area that Apple tricked out on the iPhone Duo is the camera. Not necessarily the hardware — it has the same primary lens as the iPhone 17e — but the Camera app.

For example, one of the new features is called Smart Take. You prop up the phone by folding it in half, already a useful feature, and enable Smart Take to intelligently take photos.

Smart Take looks for poses. When it sees you strike a pose or freeze, it will take a picture for you.

Smart Take looks for you to freeze in a pose before taking a photo. It takes multiple photos and tries to avoid duplicates.

It doesn't just take one though, it continuously takes them until you turn it off. This is smart too, and attempts to avoid duplicate poses.

Holding iPhone Duo in one hand with the Kid Cue interface on the front display

There's also Kid Cue, which shows a colorful Snoopy animation on the exterior screen. It's perfect to draw a child's attention just long enough to snap your picture.

My son loves Snoopy and is notoriously terrible at posing for photos. This feature seems tailor-made for my family.

Using the iPhone Duo preview mode while taking a photo

Duo Preview puts a preview of the photo you're trying to take on both the inside screen and the front screen. That way, the person in the photo can see it too.

Thinking about the times my wife and I got photos but the person taking the photo framed it wrong, I need this feature. It would save so many retakes, or my partner being disappointed that the photo wasn't framed properly.

Unlike the iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo also manages to support Cinematic Mode. The under-screen FaceTime camera makes family video calls more personal too thanks to the dual displays.

All about the software

The camera tricks are just part of the amazing software work Apple has done. My worry was Apple was going to make a foldable that essentially ran iOS on the outside, and switched to a morphed version of iPadOS on the inside.

Holding iPhone Duo in one hand

If we look at any of the "max" iPhones, it's clear Apple has a history of not really taking advantage of the larger screen size. It basically just scales everything up to fit the larger display.

That's not the case for iPhone Duo. The device runs iOS but has a refreshed interface on the outside and inside that makes sense for this form factor.

When the iPhone Duo opens and closes, the screens animate in-between

For example, the dock has moved to the edge of the phone, where your thumb will naturally rest. When you open it, it has this gorgeous animation of the front screen dissolving away to reveal the screen on the inside.

Seated view can easily show you the time when off, or different interfaces when in apps

The phone also has different use cases and features based on how it is placed. If you sit it down seated, you can watch a video with easy controls below.

This half-folded position was super comfortable for using a keyboard too. The keyboard is slightly larger, because of the phone orientation, and my typing was super fast.

If you fold the phone slightly, it automatically goes into a split mode, which is going to come in very handy. Even at this event I found myself wanting the iPhone Duo for getting work done.

A split-screen app interface would allow me to upload video in real time to both TikTok and YouTube at the same time. If you tap between the apps, you can pin them together so I could multitask between those apps and everything else I was working on.

Vertical StandBy mode with three widgets on the left, and one large widget on the right

If you take that slightly folded version and place it on a table while turned off, it goes into a larger, vertical StandBy mode. This has a lot more screen real estate for your widgets and Apple even adjusts the color too to be comfortable on the eyes.

iPhone Duo in StandBy mode with a sleek, bespoke calendar view

Placed tented, there are a lot more StandBy mode options that look stunning. I want to know where these interfaces have been in the existing StandBy mode!

There is a calendar view that has a soft white background with all the dates displayed, but behind all the numbers is the current date in a crimson red. It feels like a vintage calendar.

Portrait photo with the time displayed in StandBy mode

I saw a portrait photo mode for StandBy that caught my eye. It's like the portrait face on Apple Watch, but as a small desktop display.

If you use the iPhone Duo in this StandBy mode at night, the inside of the phone will softly glow in the morning when you go to turn off your alarm. There are so many of these little touches that I encountered, even after just a short bit with the phone.

Another concern for me was around Touch ID. Like where it is on the iPad on the power button, it doesn't always work reliably for me, probably thanks to a scar on my index finger.

So having to rely on that every time was going to be a tough sell. Apple worked around it.

If you have an Apple Watch, it will authenticate your iPhone Duo for you, so you don't need to use Face ID or Touch ID to unlock your phone. This is brilliant, and a great example of Apple devices working together.

Such a tough call

I'm still on the fence about what I want my daily driver to be. I've been a big iPhone Air user, but I use the iPhone 17 Pro for a lot of the camera abilities.

The iPhone Duo has similar compromises, but is a bit better on the camera front. In that regards, it may do just enough that I feel comfortable with it as my main device.

Split screen multitasking for iPhone Duo

I know that at least right now, after having the device in my hand, it's much better than I anticipated. It feels polished, and intuitive. I love the idea of split screen apps on a device like this and it will be helpful for the kind of work I do.

It's a big jump up in price, and certainly not perfect, but it's a very impressive first-generation device. I think it's going hard to find out of the gate.

The iPhone Duo will go up for preorder starting on October 16 starting at $1,999. Shipments start on October 23.

items.title: Before you use Apple Upgrade for iPhone 18 Pro, unlock your credit
items.summary: A credit freeze could make getting an iPhone 18 Pro on preorder day in a timely fashion much harder than it needs to be. Here's how to avoid a checkout headache.
items.content_html:
A credit freeze could make getting an iPhone 18 Pro on preorder day in a timely fashion much harder than it needs to be. Here's how to avoid a checkout headache.

Some payment options that Apple or carriers provide require a credit check before customers can complete their iPhone purchase. Anyone with frozen credit needs to plan accordingly before preorders start.

A credit freeze prevents lenders from accessing your credit report, helping stop unauthorized accounts from being created. While it won't affect existing credit cards, it can block credit checks for new financing even from vendors you already have a relationship with.

The Apple Upgrade program uses financing provided by Klarna, which requires credit approval at the time of purchase. If your credit is frozen, it will lead to automatic rejection until you lift the freeze.

Yes, even if you already have a Klarna account.

Proactively lifting a credit freeze before ordering can help keep the approval process moving. After the necessary credit check is completed, you can freeze your report again.

items.title: iPhone Duo won't work with every MagSafe accessory, and that's okay
items.summary: Yes, the iPhone Duo has MagSafe. It will not be widely compatible with the accessories we already own, and love, and that's okay.
items.content_html:
Yes, the iPhone Duo has MagSafe. It will not be widely compatible with the accessories we already own, and love, and that's okay.

On September 9, 2026, Apple's new CEO, John Ternus, hit us with a "One More Thing" that, at least everyone at AppleInsider, saw coming:

The iPhone Duo.

Apple's first foldable. A squat little smartphone that looks like the result of putting the iPhone mini and the iPad mini in the machine from the 1986 Cronenberg horror flick "The Fly."

I've known about the iPhone Duo's squat form factor for a while, and I'm a fan. You might remember me as "the AppleInsider staffer who has endlessly complained that Apple canned the iPhone mini."

The iPhone Duo, if not for the $1999 price tag, is actually something I'd be interested in getting. Especially because it's going to work with the Apple Pencil.

When I looked at the iPhone Duo, I didn't really see an iPhone in the traditional sense. Which is probably why I didn't immediately stop to think about how the iPhone Duo's form factor could be a problem for existing iPhone-compatible accessories.

Casetify is getting ready to launch iPhone Duo cases

Specifically, I'm talking about MagSafe wallets and MagSafe batteries.

Currently, there aren't a ton of MagSafe batteries that are going to work well with the iPhone Duo. There's just no space between the ring and the camera island, and/or they will hang over the bottom of the device.

Apple will come out with a first-party solution in the future, probably, like it did for iPhone Air. Other companies will come up with a sleek little square you slap on the back.

That will happen. There is going to be a huge market for batteries that work with the three-screen device, without compromise.

It's the MagSafe wallet market that I'm less sure about. I don't have an iPhone Duo in hand to test it with.

What I do have, however, is access to a US passport, which Apple has said is fairly similar in size to the iPhone Duo. Based on the size of a credit card compared to a U.S. passport, I don't think a MagSafe wallet is going to fit onto the iPhone Duo, thanks to the camera bump. Even if it did, you'd have to pull it off anyway to get your card out.

Here's more proof: Apple has chosen to exclude the iPhone Duo from the list of compatible devices on the official MagSafe Wallet listing.

Nary an iPhone Duo to be found

Wes says it could be possible if a third-party accessory developer really wanted to make it happen. He pointed out that there may be a way to make one work horizontally.

To which I replied "Well, that would look dumb as hell." And I stand by that statement, given what we're seeing for sale by some vendors on Amazon with too many adjacent consonants in their name right now.

But also you don't actually need to put a wallet on the back of your phone. As it turns out, the iPhone has existed for roughly 19 years, and MagSafe only made its first appearance in 2020.

We've been toting around things long before either of those came into existence. I trust that the average person could probably figure out how to carry both a phone and a credit card at the same time.

You could carry a separate wallet. You could go wallet-free if you're just doing your daily errands to places that take Apple Pay.

You could just throw your cards directly into the bottom of your bag and hope for the best. I don't recommend doing that, but you could.

Point being, you've got options. You don't have to eat the bean soup if you don't like beans.

Bean soup theory

The internet has led to a new theory being crafted. A theory affectionately referred to as the Bean Soup Theory.

The origin of the term is as follows: A crunchy granola girl posted a recipe for bean soup with her followers. While many people thought the recipe was great, seemingly more people arrived to yell about how they didn't like beans, and therefore demanded the recipe be augmented for them.

I'd still be willing to bet that the iPhone Duo is less divisive than the average bowl of bean soup

I'm not sure why it didn't occur to thousands of people that if they don't like beans, they don't need to make bean soup. Especially because that specific recipe was almost entirely beans.

But it's not just bean soup recipes that get bean souped. It's everything.

Pretty much anything that catches the attention of social media or YouTube will inevitably draw out people who feel compelled to comment on it. And yes, I'm aware of the irony, considering I'm AppleInsider's resident crank.

But ultimately, it boils down to is this:

Not everything is for you. Or for me. And that's okay!

If a specific accessory doesn't work for the iPhone Duo, that might just be something you learn to live with. If that incompatibility prevents you from dropping over two grand on a novelty smartphone, that may also be something you need to learn to live with.

As of right now, Apple makes six smartphones you can either currently purchase or purchase in the near future.

  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone 17e
  • iPhone 16

If you don't like something in that list, there are hundreds of other smartphones for you to choose from. Sure, Apple would prefer if you bought from them, but you don't have to. You could even just keep the iPhone you have. You don't need to buy something.

If there's anything you take away from here, it's this: The world is your oyster. The iPhone Duo might not be your pearl.

items.title: Apple Health & Quest team up for $119 blood panel
items.summary: The upgraded Apple Health experience can pull from hundreds of data points, but if you don't have recent lab results to provide, a Quest panel can be ordered through the app without getting a doctor's order.
items.content_html:
The upgraded Apple Health experience can pull from hundreds of data points, but if you don't have recent lab results to provide, a Quest panel can be ordered through the app without getting a doctor's order.

Apple Health will soon get new features built around Apple Intelligence. Every data point that can be included will help provide a holistic view of your health, but not everyone has ease of access to medical labs.

If you've already got a medical provider and had labs done recently, they may already be in Apple Health through Health Records, or can be provided via PDF. For everyone else, Apple has partnered with Quest Diagnostics to provide a comprehensive set of labs, on demand.

The service can be found and ordered in the new Apple Health experience when it launches later in 2026. It will cost $119 for a panel that pulls over 50 biomarkers.

The labs will be performed at one of 2,000 locations found across the United States. It's a much cheaper option than ordering the labs manually, especially if you don't have active insurance.

Apple Health's Lab Results tab was already quite comprehensive and included desired levels and explanations. The lab results Apple Health looks for will require blood work, urinalysis, and body measurements.

The information listed in the UI shown during the event suggests quite the range of biomarkers. They are:

  • Blood Health
  • Cardiac
  • Cholesterol
  • Glucose
  • Kidney
  • Liver
  • Blood Pressure
  • Body Metrics

Quest doesn't have locations in every state, so some may need to travel to get the labs done. If the distance becomes too cost-prohibitive, look into getting labs done at a local clinic.

The $119 can also be paid using HSA or FSA funds, though that may or may not cover the included $6 physician service fee.

Once the Quest labs are done, they'll automatically be populated in the Apple Health app. These results can be useful for understanding your overall health, and will be an excellent data point for Apple's new AI-powered health app.

The Quest labs also include an optional doctor consultation to review results.
